title: Correct metering for requests routed through opaque proxies and content-length rewrites
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: We are seeing systematic token-count discrepancies for traffic that traverses opaque middleboxes (corporate proxies, CDN edge rewrites, TLS-terminating reverse proxies) and transport-level transformations (chunked transfer-encoding coalescing, gzip/deflate injection/stripping). The current metering pipeline assumes the request body and frame boundaries it receives from the front-line ingress reflect the original client payload. When intermediaries rewrite content-length, remove or add sideband headers, or coalesce websocket/SSE fragments, we observe both overcharges (duplicate fragments counted twice) and undercharges (final emitted tokens not attributable to any input credits).

Impact: Customer-reported billing discrepancies and internal accounting alerts. Affected traffic patterns include: enterprise customers behind corporate proxies, clients using HTTP proxies that rewrite chunk boundaries (e.g., some mobile carriers), and edge CDN features that inject metadata into requests. Estimated surface: ~0.7% of hosted API billing volume for March cohort, but concentrated in high-value enterprise tenants — risk = medium.

Goals: 1) Make metering resilient to transport- and proxy-induced transformations. 2) Ensure deterministic, auditable token attribution for streaming and non-streaming requests that traverse intermediate rewrites. 3) Provide detectable heuristics and conservative fallback charging when canonicalization is impossible.

Non-goals: Revamp billing model or pricing. This ticket focuses on correctness and attribution; refunds or customer-facing credits are follow-ups.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Ava M: Spike showed mismatches are correlated with X-Forwarded-For header mutations and presence of 'Content-Encoding' toggles at the edge. Collected sample traces from affected customers (IDs redacted) and uploaded to secure bucket.

2026-03-11 — Ravi P: Implemented replay harness to simulate proxy coalescing and gzip toggling. Found two failure modes: (A) coalesced frames produce repeated tokenization of overlapping bytes, (B) proxies that strip trailing chunk markers make final fragment appear shorter, causing us to attribute fewer output tokens than generated.

2026-03-12 — Eng sync: Decision to add a canonicalization layer in ingress (edge canonicalizer) that reconstructs a best-effort original payload and emits a canonical checksum per request. Also agreed to add a 'metering-approx' flag for cases we cannot canonicalize, and to surface a reason code for downstream billing.

2026-03-12 — Design review: PM and legal want conservative charging on ambiguous fragments (bill minimum of either reconstructed claim or actual emitted tokens, whichever yields lower charge) for enterprise customers for first two weeks post-rollout.

2026-03-13 — Ravi P: PR opened with unit tests for chunked->normalized frames and a new canonicalization util module. Integration tests with a test Envoy instance pending; added telemetry counters for 'canonicalization.success' and 'canonicalization.heuristic_applied'.
implementation_notes: High-level plan: 1) Ingress canonicalizer: best-effort reassembly of chunked transfer and SSE/WebSocket fragments; normalize Content-Encoding changes (decompress if safe to do so), compute SHA256 checksum of reconstructed payload and attach X-RW-Canonical-SHA header. 2) Tokenization pass in metering: prefer checksum-based lookup to reuse previous tokenization for retried/duplicate fragments; if checksum absent, run tokenizer on canonicalized payload. 3) Metering flags: emit metering.provenance with values {direct, canonicalized, heuristic, unknown} and reason_code for diagnostics. 4) Billing policy: conservative_charge = min(tokens_from_canonicalized_payload, tokens_emitted); for enterprise tenants in the first rollout window apply conservative charge with auditing. 5) Backfill script: run discrepancy detector over last 30 days for tenants that match proxy signature and raise tickets for dependent refunds if variance > 5%.
qa_plan: Unit tests for chunk reassembly, gzip toggles, and websocket coalescing. Integration test harness with Envoy and a simulated corporate proxy that rewrites chunk boundaries. Replay e2e with real sample traces (sanitized). Add chaos tests that randomly drop frame boundaries and verify idempotent checksum and canonicalization flags. Post-deploy: monitor canonicalization.success rate (>99% target) and discrepancy ratio (<0.5% expected).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy ingress canonicalizer as opt-in header on staging; run for 100% staging traffic. Phase 2: Canary to 5% of tenants (prefer customers that reported issues); apply conservative charging for this group. Phase 3: extend to all hosted API traffic with conservative charging disabled after 14-day monitoring window if discrepancy metrics within thresholds. Rollback: disable canonicalizer header and revert metering path to previous behavior and automatically flag all canary customers for manual review.
follow_ups: PM-4042 - Customer refund automation for proxy-caused discrepancies
ENG-320900 - Add dedupe lookup table to billing to avoid double counting retried fragments
DES-2130 - Console UX: surface meter provenance and reason_code on per-request detail view
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canonicalization module passes unit + integration tests. 2) Canonical checksum present for >98% of requests that pass through known proxy signatures. 3) Discrepancy ratio between emitted tokens and canonical tokens reduced to <0.5% for canary tenants. 4) No more than 1% increase in p95 ingress latency for avg request size <64KB. 5) Audit log contains provenance and reason_code for every metered request.
notes: Edge cases: 1) Encrypted payloads where ingress cannot safely decompress — mark as 'heuristic' and do conservative billing. 2) Multipart/mime attachments: canonicalization currently applies only to text/plain and application/json request bodies; attachments deferred to follow-up. 3) For Private deployments, document a configuration toggle to opt out of canonicalization for air-gapped networks.
estimated_cost_notes: Compute: small increase from tokenization at ingress (~0.3 CPU-ms/request) and optional decompression; expected infra cost <0.5% of monthly hosted infra bill. Operational: 1 SRE on-call for first two weeks of canary.
